rationale: SUPERSEDED BEHAVIOUR UPDATED 2026-10-18 (Lead ruling task-9, per-fixture adjudication): the analyzer is ADJUDICATED CORRECT — pinned by the PASSING siblings java/module-info and java/jpms-module-exports and by the analyzer's emitJavaModuleDeclaration header — so the expectation is updated instead of the analyzer reverted. WHAT WAS SUPERSEDED AND WHY: (1) the `imports` dependency row is labelled `module_requires` (not `module_requires_dependency`) and carries isModuleRequires/isTransitive/isStatic + fileLevel + reasonCode, the spellings the sibling `module-info` pins; (2) the mandatory `references` MENTION beside every directive is labelled `module_requires_mention` / `module_exports_mention` — the same two-label-per-directive rule the siblings pin for imports and exports: `imports`/`exports` is the DEPENDENCY, `references` is the MENTION; (3) an `exports P` directive now ALSO emits the `exports` edge `module -> P` (module_exports) — the fixture's stale FORBID of that row asserted it could not exist, which is the opposite of the measured contract that sibling java/jpms-module-exports pins. COVERAGE IS NOT WEAKENED: every directive shape is still pinned, the two stale import/reference expectations are replaced by the full mention+exports expectation set, symbols are now asserted (module + its exported-package namespaces), and the two `to`-clause forbids that keep an export from being read as a dependency REMAIN. The old rationale's claim that an exports-labelled JPMS edge would be 'dropped by parallel-indexer' is superseded by measurement: the module exports edges are emitted and resolve.

forbidRelationships.comment: a `requires_modifier` is not a dependency target: the directive's target is its `module` FIELD — unchanged by this update
same: `requires static` is a modifier, not a module — unchanged
`exports P` (JLS 7.7.2) publishes this module's API OUTWARD; it is not a dependency on P — unchanged, and the reason the export rides `exports` and the dependency rides `imports`
a `to`-clause names a module that may READ this one, not one this module reads — unchanged
the module's own name is not a mention target of its directives — unchanged
